img-cns-normal.intro: This is how you'll actually see the brain: a midline sagittal view for orientation, then axial slices scrolling from the top of the head down to the foramen magnum. Find the structures you learned on the drawings in Neuroanatomy; many are organs at risk.

plates.title: Midline Sagittal
plates.caption: Midline sagittal T1 MRI of a normal adult brain (anterior on the left). Source: OpenNeuro ds003653 (Manelis A et al.), 3T MRI of a healthy adult volunteer, CC0 public domain.

hotspots.label: Corpus Callosum
hotspots.blurb: Connects the hemispheres. GBM and lymphoma can cross it ('butterfly' lesion).

hotspots.label: Thalamus
hotspots.blurb: Sensory relay. Deep, unresectable location: often biopsy then chemoRT.

hotspots.label: Pituitary Gland (Sella Turcica)
hotspots.blurb: In the sella below the optic chiasm. Pituitary dose causes late hypopituitarism.

hotspots.label: Optic Chiasm
hotspots.blurb: Just above the pituitary. OAR: ~54 Gy conventional; ≤8–10 Gy single-fraction SRS.

hotspots.label: Pineal Gland
hotspots.blurb: Pineal tumors (germ cell tumors) compress the tectum: Parinaud syndrome (upgaze palsy) and hydrocephalus.

hotspots.label: Midbrain
hotspots.blurb: Top of the brainstem; contains the cerebral aqueduct.

hotspots.label: Pons
hotspots.blurb: Diffuse midline glioma (DIPG) in children lives here: RT 54 Gy is the main treatment.

hotspots.label: Medulla
hotspots.blurb: Continues into the spinal cord at the foramen magnum.

hotspots.label: 4th Ventricle
hotspots.blurb: Behind the pons. Posterior fossa tumors (medulloblastoma, ependymoma) block it → hydrocephalus.

hotspots.label: Cerebellum (Vermis)
hotspots.blurb: Midline vermis lesions cause truncal ataxia.

plates.title: Level 1: Centrum Semiovale (High Convexity)
plates.caption: Axial T1 MRI above the lateral ventricles (patient's right on your left). Source: OpenNeuro ds003653 (Manelis A et al.), 3T MRI of a healthy adult volunteer, CC0 public domain.

hotspots.label: Centrum Semiovale (White Matter)
hotspots.blurb: Big sheet of white matter above the ventricles. Radiation leukoencephalopathy shows up here as bright FLAIR signal.

hotspots.label: Falx Cerebri
hotspots.blurb: Dural fold between the hemispheres. Parafalcine meningiomas arise here; midline shift is measured against it.

hotspots.label: Superior Sagittal Sinus
hotspots.blurb: Venous sinus at the top of the falx. Parasagittal meningiomas can invade it (limits resection).

hotspots.label: Cortex (Gray Matter)
hotspots.blurb: Metastases favor the gray-white junction.

plates.title: Level 2: Bodies of the Lateral Ventricles
plates.caption: Axial T2 MRI through the bodies of the lateral ventricles (CSF is bright). Source: OpenNeuro ds003653 (Manelis A et al.), 3T MRI of a healthy adult volunteer, CC0 public domain.

hotspots.label: Lateral Ventricle (Body)
hotspots.blurb: CSF-filled. Periventricular enhancement suggests lymphoma or ependymal spread.

hotspots.label: Corpus Callosum (Body)
hotspots.blurb: Crossing tumor = GBM or lymphoma until proven otherwise.

hotspots.label: Caudate Nucleus (Body)
hotspots.blurb: Lines the lateral wall of the lateral ventricle.

hotspots.label: Corona Radiata
hotspots.blurb: White matter fanning out toward the cortex.

hotspots.label: Septum Pellucidum
hotspots.blurb: Thin midline membrane between the lateral ventricles.

plates.title: Level 3: Basal Ganglia & Thalamus
plates.caption: Axial T1 MRI at the level of the basal ganglia and thalami (CSF is dark). Source: OpenNeuro ds003653 (Manelis A et al.), 3T MRI of a healthy adult volunteer, CC0 public domain.

hotspots.label: Frontal Horn
hotspots.blurb: Front of the lateral ventricle.

hotspots.label: Head of Caudate
hotspots.blurb: Bulges into the frontal horn.

hotspots.label: Internal Capsule
hotspots.blurb: Motor and sensory fibers in a tight bundle. A small lesion here causes dense contralateral weakness.

hotspots.label: Lentiform Nucleus (Putamen + Globus Pallidus)
hotspots.blurb: Lateral to the internal capsule.

hotspots.label: Thalamus
hotspots.blurb: Behind the internal capsule, beside the 3rd ventricle.

hotspots.label: 3rd Ventricle
hotspots.blurb: Midline slit.

hotspots.label: Insula
hotspots.blurb: Deep cortex under the Sylvian fissure; insular gliomas are hard to resect (MCA branches).

hotspots.label: Occipital Horn
hotspots.blurb: Back of the lateral ventricle.

plates.title: Level 4: Midbrain & Suprasellar Cistern
plates.caption: Axial T1 MRI through the midbrain and suprasellar cistern. Source: OpenNeuro ds003653 (Manelis A et al.), 3T MRI of a healthy adult volunteer, CC0 public domain.

hotspots.label: Cerebral Peduncles
hotspots.blurb: Front of the midbrain: descending motor fibers.

hotspots.label: Cerebral Aqueduct
hotspots.blurb: Tiny CSF channel at the back of the midbrain.

hotspots.label: Optic Chiasm / Suprasellar Cistern
hotspots.blurb: Star-shaped CSF space in front of the midbrain; the chiasm sits in it. Pituitary macroadenomas push up into it.

hotspots.label: Hippocampus (Temporal Horn)
hotspots.blurb: Medial temporal lobe. Spared in HA-WBRT (D100% ≤9 Gy, Dmax ≤16 Gy in 10 fx).

hotspots.label: Temporal Lobe
hotspots.blurb: Temporal lobe necrosis is a late risk with skull base/nasopharynx RT.

hotspots.label: Middle Cerebral Artery
hotspots.blurb: In the Sylvian fissure.

plates.title: Level 5: Pons & Cerebellopontine Angle
plates.caption: Axial T2 MRI through the pons and inner ears (CSF and inner-ear fluid are bright). Source: OpenNeuro ds003653 (Manelis A et al.), 3T MRI of a healthy adult volunteer, CC0 public domain.

hotspots.label: Pons
hotspots.blurb: Brainstem OAR. DIPG arises here.

hotspots.label: Cerebellopontine Angle
hotspots.blurb: Space between pons and cerebellum. Vestibular schwannomas (~80% of CPA masses) and meningiomas.

hotspots.label: Internal Auditory Canal (CN VII/VIII)
hotspots.blurb: Facial and vestibulocochlear nerves. Vestibular schwannomas start here and widen the canal.

hotspots.label: Cochlea
hotspots.blurb: Hearing OAR: mean ≤35–45 Gy conventional; ≤4 Gy for vestibular schwannoma SRS.

hotspots.label: 4th Ventricle
hotspots.blurb: Behind the pons.

hotspots.label: Cerebellar Hemisphere
hotspots.blurb: Posterior fossa mets often need surgery (hydrocephalus risk).

hotspots.label: Basilar Artery
hotspots.blurb: In front of the pons.

plates.title: Level 6: Medulla & Foramen Magnum
plates.caption: Axial T1 MRI at the foramen magnum: medulla with the cerebellar tonsils behind it. Source: OpenNeuro ds003653 (Manelis A et al.), 3T MRI of a healthy adult volunteer, CC0 public domain.

hotspots.label: Medulla
hotspots.blurb: Lowest brainstem; CN IX–XII nuclei.

hotspots.label: Cerebellar Tonsils
hotspots.blurb: Herniation through the foramen magnum is fatal; large posterior fossa masses risk it.

hotspots.label: Foramen Magnum
hotspots.blurb: Brainstem becomes spinal cord.

img-cns-special.intro: Three regions you'll plan around constantly: the sella and cavernous sinus, the orbits and optic pathway, and the spinal cord. Each holds organs at risk with strict dose limits.

plates.title: Coronal: Sella & Cavernous Sinus
plates.caption: Coronal T1 MRI of a normal pituitary gland (patient's right on your left). Source: Mannion P, Jude E, Endocrinol Diabetes Metab Case Rep 2026 (PMC13454250), Fig. 1B, CC BY 4.0.

hotspots.label: Pituitary Gland
hotspots.blurb: Sits in the sella. Adenomas: nonfunctioning or hormone-secreting (prolactin, GH, ACTH).

hotspots.label: Cavernous Sinus
hotspots.blurb: Beside the sella. Contains CN III, IV, V1, V2, VI and the internal carotid. Invasion makes surgery incomplete (RT or SRS for residual).

hotspots.label: Internal Carotid Artery (Cavernous)
hotspots.blurb: Runs through the cavernous sinus; meningiomas can encase it.

hotspots.label: Sphenoid Sinus
hotspots.blurb: The transsphenoidal surgical route to the pituitary.

hotspots.label: Temporal Lobe
hotspots.blurb: Lateral to the cavernous sinus.

plates.title: Axial: Orbits & Optic Pathway
plates.caption: Axial T2 MRI through the mid-orbits (vitreous is bright, lens is dark). Source: Nagesh CP et al., Indian J Ophthalmol 2021 (PMC8597479), Fig. 11a, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0; labels and arrows removed.

hotspots.label: Lens
hotspots.blurb: Very radiosensitive: cataract with just a few Gy (keep Dmax <7 Gy when possible).

hotspots.label: Globe / Retina
hotspots.blurb: Retina Dmax <45–50 Gy (retinopathy).

hotspots.label: Lacrimal Gland
hotspots.blurb: Upper outer orbit. Mean <26–30 Gy to avoid dry eye.

hotspots.label: Optic Nerve
hotspots.blurb: Dmax ~54 Gy conventional; blindness risk above ~55–60 Gy.

hotspots.label: Optic Chiasm
hotspots.blurb: Where nasal fibers cross.

plates.title: Sagittal Spine: Cord & Cauda Equina
plates.caption: Placeholder MRI-style slice (sagittal T2 of the thoracolumbar spine). Swap in a real de-identified MRI image here.

hotspots.label: Spinal Cord
hotspots.blurb: Dmax ~45–50 Gy conventional; SBRT limits are much lower per fraction.

hotspots.label: Conus Medullaris (L1–L2)
hotspots.blurb: Where the cord ends in adults. Compression here causes bowel/bladder dysfunction and saddle anesthesia.

hotspots.label: Cauda Equina
hotspots.blurb: Nerve roots below the conus. More tolerant than cord.

hotspots.label: Thecal Sac End (S2)
hotspots.blurb: The bottom of CSF: the inferior border for craniospinal irradiation.

hotspots.label: Vertebral Body
hotspots.blurb: Most spine metastases start here and grow back into the canal.

hotspots.label: Epidural Space
hotspots.blurb: Tumor here compresses the cord: metastatic epidural spinal cord compression (Bilsky grade).

hotspots.label: Posterior Elements
hotspots.blurb: Pedicles, lamina, spinous process.

gallery.title: HA-WBRT dose
gallery.caption: Hippocampal-avoidance whole-brain plan: the two cool spots in the middle are the spared hippocampi. Source: Yang X et al., Eur J Med Res 2023 (PMC9841677), Fig. 1B, CC BY 4.0.

gallery.title: Craniospinal field
gallery.caption: VMAT craniospinal plan (sagittal): the whole brain and spinal canal down to the thecal sac are treated. Source: Agdi B et al., Cureus 2026 (PMC13354313), Fig. 3, CC BY 4.0.

img-cns-glioma.intro: Gliomas are read on two sequences side by side: T1 post-contrast (enhancing tumor) and T2/FLAIR (edema and infiltrative tumor). High-grade gliomas enhance; most low-grade gliomas don't.

gallery.title: Glioblastoma: T1 Post-Contrast
gallery.caption: Axial T1 post-contrast MRI: left temporal glioblastoma with a thick, irregular enhancing rim around a necrotic center. Source: Armed Forces Institute of Pathology (Wikimedia Commons, AFIP-00405558), public domain. Look for: Thick Irregular Ring Enhancement; Central Necrosis; Compressed Ventricle.

gallery.title: Glioblastoma: FLAIR
gallery.caption: Axial FLAIR MRI of a different patient: left temporal glioblastoma with extensive surrounding FLAIR signal and mass effect. Source: Tiwari S, Gyawali I, Cureus 2024 (PMC10944577), Fig. 5B, CC BY 4.0. Look for: FLAIR Hyperintensity (Edema + Infiltrating Tumor); Tumor Core; Effaced Sulci; Normal Contralateral Hemisphere.

gallery.title: Low-Grade Glioma: FLAIR (Non-Enhancing)
gallery.caption: Axial FLAIR MRI: grade 2 astrocytoma in the left anterior insula and frontal white matter, non-enhancing. Source: Vail M et al., Cureus 2026 (PMC12947947), Fig. 3, CC BY 4.0; arrow removed. Look for: Homogeneous FLAIR-Bright Mass; Cortical Involvement; Mild Mass Effect.

img-cns-mets.intro: Brain metastases are the most common tumors you'll treat with radiation. Contrast MRI (thin slices) finds them and plans them.

gallery.title: Brain Metastases: T1 Post-Contrast
gallery.caption: Axial T1 post-contrast MRI: many small enhancing brain metastases from lung cancer. Source: Hellerhoff (Wikimedia Commons, BC - Hirnmetastasen MRT T1KM ax), CC BY-SA 3.0. Look for: Met at the Gray-White Junction; Punctate Met.

gallery.title: SRS Plan: Targets & Dose
gallery.caption: Fractionated SRS plan: left frontal resection cavity (24 Gy in 3 fractions) and a right-sided intact metastasis, axial (left) and coronal (right); prescription isodose in green, low-dose spill in blue, optic structures in orange. Source: Lewis J et al., Cureus 2025 (PMC12414254), Fig. 2A, CC BY 4.0; orientation letters removed. Look for: GTV = Enhancing Lesion (±1 mm PTV); Prescription Isodose Line; 12 Gy Volume (V12); Optic Nerves / Chiasm; Resection Cavity.

img-cns-benign.intro: Benign tumors are a big part of CNS radiation: meningiomas, vestibular schwannomas, and pituitary adenomas. Each has a signature look.

gallery.title: Meningioma: T1 Post-Contrast
gallery.caption: Coronal T1 post-contrast MRI: homogeneously enhancing parasagittal meningioma. Source: James Heilman, MD (Wikimedia Commons, MRIMeningioma), CC BY-SA 4.0; arrow removed. Look for: Homogeneously Enhancing Extra-axial Mass; CSF Cleft.

gallery.title: Vestibular Schwannoma: T1 Post-Contrast
gallery.caption: Axial T1 post-contrast MRI: right vestibular schwannoma at the cerebellopontine angle (patient's right on your left). Source: Hellerhoff (Wikimedia Commons, Akustikus-Schwannom rechts MRT T1KM axial 001), CC BY-SA 3.0. Look for: Intracanalicular Part (Cone); Cisternal Part (Scoop); Brainstem / Pons; 4th Ventricle.

gallery.title: Pituitary Macroadenoma: Coronal T1
gallery.caption: Coronal T1 post-contrast MRI: pituitary macroadenoma expanding the sella and rising into the suprasellar cistern to abut the optic chiasm. Source: Iyer C et al., JCEM Case Rep 2026 (PMC13198944), Fig. 1A, CC BY 4.0; arrow removed. Look for: Macroadenoma (≥1 cm); Optic Chiasm (Compressed); Internal Carotid Artery; Sphenoid Sinus.

img-cns-advanced.intro: CT is the first scan in the ER and the planning scan; advanced MRI and PET help separate tumor from treatment effect after RT.

gallery.title: CT Head: What to Look For
gallery.caption: Non-contrast axial CT: acute left basal ganglia hemorrhage (bright) with surrounding hypodense edema. Source: Elsherif Y et al., Radiol Case Rep 2025 (PMC12098020), Fig. 6, CC BY 4.0. Look for: Acute Hemorrhage (Bright); Hypodense Edema.

gallery.title: After Treatment: Progression or Treatment Effect?
gallery.caption: Treated glioblastoma with a new enhancing lesion (left: T1 post-contrast) that was pathology-proven radiation necrosis; perfusion map (right) shows the lesion is not hyperperfused. Source: Mohamedbaqer Easa A et al., Cureus 2025 (PMC12393895), Fig. 2A-B, CC BY 4.0; circles and panel letters removed. Look for: New/Growing Enhancement; Perfusion (rCBV).

gallery.title: MRI Spine: Cord Compression
gallery.caption: Sagittal T2 MRI of the thoracic spine: pathologic T5 fracture from metastatic rectal cancer with epidural extension compressing the cord. Source: Kuah T et al., Cancers 2022 (PMC9265325), Fig. 10a, CC BY 4.0. Look for: Vertebral Body Metastasis; Epidural Tumor; Compressed Spinal Cord; CSF Around the Cord.
